questions.question:
Fill in the blank with most appropriate tense:
The train ___ before we reached the station.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**had left**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The sentence describes two past events: one (the train leaving) occurred before the other (reaching the station).
 
• To indicate the earlier of two past events, the **past perfect tense** is used for the earlier action.
 
• The structure for the past perfect tense is **"had + past participle."**
 
• **Options 1, 2,** and **4** are incorrect because they do not use the past perfect tense, which is required for this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The train **had left**__ before we reached the station."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "left"** is incorrect because it is in the simple past tense, which does not indicate the sequence of the two past actions.
 
• **Option 2: "leaves"** is incorrect because it is in the present tense, which is inconsistent with the past context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "will leave"** is incorrect because it is in the future tense, which is also inconsistent with the past context.
</ul

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with most appropriate option:
Hardly had she entered the room ___ the phone rang.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**when**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The sentence uses the conjunction "**Hardly**," which is often followed by "**when**" to indicate two events happening in quick succession.
 
• The correct structure for such sentences is: "**Hardly + had + subject + past participle + when + subject + verb (past simple).**"
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and **4** do not fit the grammatical structure and meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Hardly had she entered the room **when**__ the phone rang."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "than"** is incorrect because "than" is used in comparative sentences, not with "hardly."
 
• **Option 3: "then"** is incorrect as it is used to indicate a sequence of events, not in this grammatical structure.
 
• **Option 4: "while"** is incorrect because "while" indicates simultaneous actions, which does not match the intended meaning here.
</ul

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

He has been living (1) / on this street (2) / since five years. (3) / with his family(4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the preposition "**since**" before the phrase "**five years**."
 
• The preposition "**for**" is used to indicate a period or duration of time (e.g., for two months, for a long time).
 
• Conversely, "**since**" is used to indicate a specific starting point in time (e.g., since 2019, since Monday).
 
• Because "five years" is a duration, the correct phrase should be "**for five years**," ensuring grammatical correctness.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He has been living on this street **for five** years with his family."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "He has been living" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and appropriately uses the present perfect continuous tense.
 
• **2: "on this street"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and uses the appropriate preposition for a street.
 
• **4: "with his family."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is a lack of parallelism in verb tenses, specifically the incorrect use of the present tense verb "**catch**" in part 4.
 
• The conjunction "**and**" joins two actions in this sentence. For grammatical consistency, both verbs should be in the same tense.
 
• Since the first action occurred in the past ("**ran into**"), the subsequent action must also be in the simple past tense.
 
• Therefore, the phrase "catch up" needs to be changed to "**caught up**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"We ran into some old friends at the mall **and caught** up."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "We ran into" **– This part of the sentence correctly uses the simple past tense of the phrasal verb "run into," meaning to meet unexpectedly.
 
• **2: "some old friends"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and functions perfectly as the object of the verb.
 
• **3: "at the mall"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and correctly uses the preposition "at" for a specific location.

• "She picked it up."

questions.question:
Arrange the passage correctly:
(1) Pull the safety pin of the fire extinguisher.
(2) Aim the nozzle of the pipe at the base of the fire.
(3) Squeeze the handle to release the agent.
(4) Sweep the nozzle from side to side.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The proper sequence for using a fire extinguisher is summarized by the acronym **P.A.S.S.**, which stands for Pull, Aim, Squeeze, and Sweep.
 
• **Step 1: Pull** the safety pin of the fire extinguisher to break the tamper seal and enable its use.
 
• **Step 2: Aim** the nozzle at the base of the fire where the fuel source is located, not the flames.
 
• **Step 3: Squeeze** the handle to release the extinguishing agent.
 
• **Step 4: Sweep** the nozzle from side to side to cover the base of the fire and extinguish it effectively.
 
• According to this sequence, the correct order is: **1 - 2 - 3 - 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fire Safety Tips:**
 
 
• Ensure the fire extinguisher is appropriate for the type of fire (e.g., Class A, B, C, or D).
 
• Keep the extinguisher in an easily accessible location and ensure it is regularly inspected.
 
• Do not attempt to fight a fire if it is too large or spreading rapidly; evacuate the area and call emergency services immediately.
 
 
 
• **Types of Fire Extinguishers:**
 
 
• **Water Extinguishers:** Suitable for Class A fires (wood, paper, etc.).
 
• **Foam Extinguishers:** Effective for Class A and B fires (flammable liquids).
 
• **CO2 Extinguishers:** Best for electrical fires and flammable liquids.
 
• **Dry Powder Extinguishers:** Versatile and used for Class A, B, and C fires.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Arrange the passage correctly:**

(1) Push the door open.

(2) The door unlocks with a click.

(3) Turn the key clockwise.

(4) Insert the key in the lock.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1)** i.e. **4 - 3 - 2 - 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sequence follows the **chronological logic** of opening a locked door. The process must begin by **inserting the key (4)** into the lock.
 
• After the key is inserted, the physical action required to engage the mechanism is to **turn the key (3)**.
 
• The immediate result of turning the key is that the locking bolt retracts, which is when **the door unlocks with a click (2)**.
 
• Only after the lock is fully disengaged can you perform the final step and **push the door open (1)**.

Therefore, the correct logical order is **4 - 3 - 2 - 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (3-4-2-1):** This is physically impossible because you cannot turn a key before it has been inserted into the lock.
 
• **Option 3 (4-2-3-1):** This suggests the door clicks and unlocks before the turning action happens, which reverses cause and effect.
 
• **Option 4 (2-3-4-1):** This implies the door is already unlocked before you even touch the key, making the insertion and turning steps redundant.

questions.question:
Fill in the correct collocation in the following sentence.

I wish to ______ my own cafe one day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**3**' i.e. 'have'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is about expressing a desire or ambition for the future.
 
• The correct collocation to use with the verb "wish" in this context is "**have**," which indicates ownership or possession.
 
• **Options 1, 2,** and **4** are grammatically incorrect in this context:
 
 
• **Option 1: "made"** is incorrect because it refers to past tense and does not fit the future intention expressed in the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "make"** is incorrect because it does not match the collocation "wish to have."
 
• **Option 4: "do"** is incorrect because it does not convey the meaning of ownership or possession.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"I wish to **have**__ my own cafe one day."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Collocation:** Some verbs are commonly paired with specific other words to form natural-sounding combinations, like "wish to have."
 
• **Future Intent:** The use of "wish to have" expresses a future aspiration or desire.
